Subject: Immediate: spike in 5xx/429 after Orchid v2f deploy

Jordan —

We pushed the Orchid v2f model (quantized) this morning per the scheduled rollout (11:45 PT). Since ~08:50 PT we are seeing a sustained spike in 5xx and 429s from the Redwood endpoint serving our critical inference paths (embed + chat). Error rate is ~11% across the last 20 minutes, median latency is up 3x, and clients are reporting timeouts and exponential retries.

Attached is a compressed log sample (aurora_error_log_0618.zip) showing repeated 429 floods and the client-side retry pattern. We need an immediate rollback or mitigation — this is impacting our live customers. Please advise ASAP.

Key info:
- Account: Aurora Analytics (prod)
- Host: api.redwood.com/model/orchid-v2f
- First observed: 2027-06-18T08:50:12-07:00
- Approx error breakdown: 5xx (60%), 429 (35%), timeouts (5%)

Ralph Meyer
Ops Lead, Aurora Analytics
ops@auroranalytics.com

Subject: Re: Immediate: spike in 5xx/429 after Orchid v2f deploy

Jordan / team — quick findings from the first 20 minutes of investigation: 

1) Deploy manifest shows orchid-v2f applied with kernel selector: fused-attn-v3 and quant profile: q4_0_dynamic. The previous stable was orchid-v2e with fused-attn-v2 / q8_dynamic.

2) Error signature: upstream worker logs show KV cache miss/error followed by a burst of requeue/retries. Stack traces point to the new fused-attn-v3 path hitting a race when cache size > 48k tokens/session leading to early 429s from the fronting proxy. This then amplified client-side retries (Aurora logs show exponential backoff misconfigured).

Snippet from worker log (sanitized):
> 2027-06-18T08:51:03Z ERROR serve: request failed: kv_cache->get() invalidation at idx 48921 -> fallback triggered -> http 500
> 2027-06-18T08:51:03Z WARN proxy: rate-limited (429) -> enqueue retry

3) Repro on canary node: yes, when we switch kernel to fused-attn-v2 the error does not reproduce.

Recommendation (immediate):
- Initiate rollback to orchid-v2e across the affected pool (can do automated rollback; ETA 8-12 minutes).
- While rollback is underway, enable per-customer circuit-breaker and reduce client retry ceiling for Aurora routes.
- Post-rollback: run regression harness focusing on long-session KV cache patterns and the fused-attn-v3 kernel.

I’m preparing an ops runbook for the rollback and will attach the deploy manifest excerpt (orchid-v2f-deploy-manifest.txt).

Marissa Cole
Sr. SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Team / Ralph —

Thanks for the rapid investigation. Summary for execs and next steps:

Impact:
- Customer: Aurora Analytics (prod) — critical inference traffic degraded, user-facing errors observed.
- Severity: P0 (customer-impacting, multiple tenants affected through shared pool).

Cause (initial assessment):
- Model rollout (orchid-v2f) introduced a kernel change (fused-attn-v3) + new quant profile. This path exposes a KV cache race when token/session size exceeds previous thresholds, triggering 5xx and 429s and then client retry amplification.

Approvals requested:
1) Emergency rollback to orchid-v2e across Aurora’s pool (Marissa estimates 8–12 min).
2) Offer Aurora a one-time bill credit for the incident window while we confirm root cause and run regression tests.

I approve the rollback now. Jordan / Ben, please coordinate the customer comms and credit. Post-rollback, schedule an incident review with engineering and product; we need a mitigation plan (kernel fix or fallback) before reattempting v2f.

Evelyn Hart
VP, Customer Success
